body:
**Scope.** Surfaced by the Tier-1 (#250) and Tier-2 (#196) reconstruction scenarios. On `origin/main`, **no production path enqueues a repair obligation for a fragment that is simply absent.** Present-but-corrupt fragments and explicit losses are covered; plain absence is not:

- production scrub `continue`s on `Ok(None)` — the "a fragment that vanished between the walk and the fetch is a loss for GC/reconstruction to notice, not a checksum finding — skip it" arm (`crates/custodian/src/scrub.rs:89-92`); scrub enqueues repair only on a checksum failure (`scrub.rs:85`, `:105`);
- a killed / partitioned D server cannot be `list_fragments()`'d, so its absent fragments are never observed by the scrub walk in the first place;
- the read path appends only **present-but-corrupt** fragments to the repair set (`crates/core/src/read.rs:151`, `:158` — `corrupt.push`), not missing ones.

Because of this gap, both reconstruction fault scenarios drive the production `reconcile_step` → `reconstruction::reconcile` path via a **sanctioned test stand-in** — `repair::enqueue_repair(&meta, CHUNK, "...")` (`tier2_kill_reconstruct.rs:545`, and the new `tier1_jepsen_consistency.rs`) — to inject the obligation a real detector would produce. The reconstruction path itself is genuinely exercised; only the **detection trigger** is stubbed.

**Definition of done**
- [ ] a production path detects a simply-missing placed fragment (e.g. scrub treating `Ok(None)` on a *placed* fragment as a repair obligation) and calls `enqueue_repair`, with guardrails against false positives during in-flight writes / GC
- [ ] a regression test that fails without the detection and passes with it
- [ ] the #250 / #196 scenarios can drop the `enqueue_repair` test stand-in (or keep it only belt-and-suspenders) once real detection is wired

**Refs:** stand-in precedent #196 (`tier2_kill_reconstruct.rs:545`); #250 (Tier-1 scenario, same stand-in); `crates/custodian/src/scrub.rs:89-92`; `crates/core/src/read.rs:151-158`; proposal 0005 §reconstruction / §scrub.

milestone.description: The self-maintaining durability plane (L4): GC, scrub, reconstruction, rebalance + durability telemetry. Makes single-zone trustworthy; gates the Step-2 release. Plan: proposal 0005.

title: Custodian — no production path enqueues repair for a simply-missing fragment (missing-fragment detection gap)
